points: The Q3 print will show whether Cboe can sustain the mid-to-high-teens organic total net revenue growth target it raised after Q2, when net revenue rose 25 percent to a record $731.6 million.
It will reveal if Data Vantage is tracking toward the raised low-teens organic net revenue target, following Q2’s 15 percent year-over-year growth.

The report should confirm whether the Cboe Australia sale closed in Q3 and whether the $11 million reduction to 2026 adjusted operating expense guidance is reflected, keeping costs inside the $838–$853 million range.
Q3 will test whether the Derivatives business can keep riding record index-options demand after Q2 delivered 30 percent net revenue growth there.
With FY1 EPS consensus up 32.9 percent and FY2 up 7.1 percent, the print will show if the recent 11-up/0-down revision trend has room to lift estimates further or if growth is normalizing.
Valuation is flagged fair at roughly 1.1x theme P/E and 1.0x theme PEG, so the long case rests on Q3 results and guidance reinforcing the 2026 acceleration rather than on multiple expansion.
watch: Organic total net revenue growth stays at or above the mid-to-high-teens guidance — supports the long.
Data Vantage organic net revenue growth stays at or above the low-teens guidance — supports the long.
Adjusted operating expenses remain within the $838–$853 million guidance and reflect the $11 million Australia-related reduction — supports the long.
Derivatives net revenue growth stays strong, confirming continued index-options demand — supports the long.
